title: “POSSIBLE INITIAL CAUSES OF GAIAN-TYPE MECHANISMS”

lists.name: Possible initial causes of Gaian-type mechanisms
items: Amplification (incl. phenomena analogous to a maser, synchrotron, etc)
Analogs of the Belousov-Zhabotinskii chemical reaction
Biogenic cycles [e.g. biogeochemical cycles; the biogenic destabilization of the physical environment or 'geosphere']
Coalescence (e.g. of cycles, networks, processes, phenomena, etc)

'Coequilibrium' [def. as a tendency of two or more processes—perhaps of an opposite but complementary and reciprocally necessary character—to support and limit one another, and to dominate one or more environmental variables, to such a degree as to maintain a status quo]
Continuum between the Gaian and non-Gaian bios
Evolution and operation of active and complex biological management systems
Harmonics (subharmonics or superharmonics; coincidental or induced)
Knotting (as a special case of entanglement)

NETWORK: growth, reinforcement, self-resonance, self-reinforcement, autocorrelation, 'institutionalization', differentiation, mutation, progression, fission, budding, cellularization, 'morphodynamicization' [def. as a tendency to become a diachronic, stable morphodynamical process], etc
Partial identity [over a range—e.g. a structural, spatial, temporal, dynamical, compositional, parametric, and/or even more 'abstract' range]
Partial or exact matching of different cycles

notes: by Patrick Gunkel. FOREWORD: The concern of the present list is limited to general categories of possibilities. The photographed chart is cropped below item 58, so any subsequent material is not visible.
